summary:
We developed SxMOV (SPHEREx Moving Object Visualizer), an interactive web laboratory designed to detect and analyze celestial objects moving relative to the background stars using multi-epoch data from NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope.
SxMOV addresses the challenge of processing massive, multi-wavelength datasets by automating data retrieval from NASA/IPAC IRSA and SIMBAD. The application aligns and reprojects FITS cutouts across different observation dates, generates time-lapse animations, and performs epoch-to-epoch image subtraction—canceling static background stars to isolate moving targets such as asteroids, comets, and high-proper-motion stars. It also cross-matches sources with ESA Gaia astrometry and extracts 0.75–5 µm infrared spectra to reveal their physical composition.
By transforming complex spectroscopic archives into an accessible, zero-code visual interface with shareable observation links, SxMOV democratizes space data exploration for researchers, students, and citizen scientists worldwide.
details:
How It Works & Key Features
SxMOV (SPHEREx Moving Object Visualizer) is an interactive web platform built to detect and characterize celestial objects moving relative to background stars using multi-epoch infrared data from NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Users can search any target by catalog identifier (via SIMBAD or Sesame) or sky coordinates (RA/Dec). SxMOV queries NASA/IPAC IRSA via Simple Image Access (SIA), downloads multi-epoch FITS cutouts concurrently, and reprojects them onto a common World Coordinate System (WCS) grid.
To isolate moving targets, the tool generates customizable time-lapse GIFs and performs epoch-to-epoch image subtraction (A − B), canceling static background sources so asteroids, comets, and high-proper-motion stars stand out as positive–negative pairs. Users can overlay ESA Gaia DR3 astrometry (corrected for proper motion to each observation epoch) and extract 0.75–5 µm aperture spectra to analyze surface composition, water ice features (~3 µm), or thermal emission.
Tools, Software & Architecture
  • Programming Language & UI: Python 3 and Streamlit with custom HTML5/CSS3 styling for a mission-control HUD interface.
  • Astronomical & Scientific Libraries: Astropy (WCS, FITS handling, coordinates, time), Astroquery (IRSA, SIMBAD, Gaia), Reproject (image alignment), NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Pillow (PIL).
  • Data Sources: NASA/IPAC IRSA (SPHEREx DR/QR releases), CDS SIMBAD, and ESA Gaia DR3.
Creativity, Design & Expected Impact
Rather than presenting raw tables, SxMOV combines an educational mission hub with a Live Astrophysical Guide that automatically classifies the queried object and explains what motion and spectral signatures to look for. Our team prioritized accessibility, fault-tolerant API retries, and reproducibility via shareable observation URLs—empowering students, amateur astronomers, and researchers worldwide to explore SPHEREx data without writing code.
